Glossary

The terms this guide uses, in alphabetical order.

Action log
The local, gitignored trace of what the loop did for each goal. More.
Block
A goal waiting on another issue. Unlike a park, it clears by itself when the blocker closes. More.
Chain
One end goal plus every open prerequisite behind it, solved in order with every question asked up front. More.
Claim
A record that a session has taken a goal. A claim from a session that has died is reclaimed. More.
Design gate
An opt-in check that stops a goal with no confirmed design from being worked, parks it and files a design ticket. Off by default. More.
Dossier
A business idea captured through a fixed interview with no code exploration. The optional front end of the flow. More.
Epic
The Spec or Epic ticket created once a design is confirmed. It has the slices as children. Never picked by the loop; the slices are. More.
Goal
One issue (or goal file) that Sigma picks up and carries through the seven phases to a merged, verified pull request. It carries sdlc:goal. More.
Host
The agent environment Sigma runs in: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity. More.
Land
To carry a goal all the way through review and merge in one unattended run. /sigma-goal --land does it for one goal. More.
Ledger
The committed team record of claims and outcomes per author, so people and machines can see who is working on what. More.
Output block
One of the three fixed status formats the agent uses: Status, Event or Decision. More.
Overlay
A label that rides beside sdlc:goal to say why a goal cannot be picked yet. More.
Park
To set a goal aside, with a reason, because it needs a human. A parked goal leaves the loop's world until a person runs the unpark command. More.
Phase
One of seven steps every non-trivial goal passes through: Goal, Research, Plan, Plan-Review, Implement, Review, Retrospective. More.
Registry
The committed record of units and the goals in each, kept in the project folder. More.
Slice
One of the smaller goals a bigger piece of work is split into. A follow-up found mid-goal joins its goal as a slice by default, up to a limit.
Story
The ticket tier that holds a Dossier: pure business intent. Never picked by the loop.
Unit
A body of work several goals share a branch for. Short for unit of work. More.
Verify
Running your test command and recording the evidence. With enforcement on, a goal cannot be marked done without fresh evidence. More.
Wave
A set of goals that can run at the same time because every goal they wait on sits in an earlier wave. /sigma-orchestrate plans them. More.
